policies.policy_name: User Role and Record Relationship Verification
policies.description: The assistant must operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles and verified record relationships before performing any operation, including removing a child incident mapping.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.

policies.description: Only one validated operation may be performed at a time; the request must not proceed if required data is missing or the current record state prevents the action.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: Any request that creates, updates, or removes a record must validate that all mandatory fields are provided; for remove_child_incident at least one of the required identifiers must be present.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: The assistant must never assume or fabricate IDs; it must rely on verified API results to confirm that incident IDs and mapping IDs exist before attempting removal.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.

policies.description: Only users with the Administrator role, which has Full CRUD access across all tables, are authorized to delete a child incident mapping.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.

policies.description: Users with the Manager role have Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge) and are therefore permitted to remove a child incident mapping.
references: Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables.

policies.description: Agents have Full CRUD on Incidents and related tables, allowing them to delete child‑incident relationships.
references: Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables.

policies.policy_name: User Clarification on Missing Mandatory Fields
policies.description: If a mandatory identifier (e.g., child_incident_mapping_id, parent_incident, or child_incident) is missing, the assistant must state which field is required rather than asking for additional clarification.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: Before removing a child‑incident mapping, the assistant must ensure that removing the relationship does not violate referential integrity constraints.
references: Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.

policies.description: Users with the Reporter role are prohibited from deleting child‑incident mappings because they cannot view or modify records opened by other users.
references: Reporter (reporter) | IT Service Consumption | Can view and update their own submitted Incidents/Requests. Can search Public Knowledge articles. | Cannot view or modify records opened by other users, CMDB, or internal work notes.

policies.description: If required identifiers (e.g., child_incident_mapping_id, parent_incident, child_incident) are missing, the assistant must perform a lookup and reuse verified IDs from prior responses before proceeding.
references: When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.

policies.description: When the requesting user lacks the necessary role‑based permission to delete a child incident mapping, the operation must be aborted with a 403 Forbidden response.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.description: If a request to remove a child incident mapping violates any policy, the assistant must stop the operation and return the specific policy reason.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.description: All removal actions must be performed in a logical and efficient sequence, adhering to the overall execution flow guidelines.
references: Complete each task in a logical, and efficient execution flow.
